notes.content: A handwritten letter headed Voorschoten, March 29 1967, Palestrinalaan 11, addressed to Grothendieck. The opening reports dispatch of a manuscript on the tame fund. group in two covers together with borrowed papers. The terminology paragraph adopts scheme in stead of prescheme but awaits a decision on doublet. The References paragraph discusses EGA and the old SGA seminar numbering. The p.3 and p.5 comments explain the placement of Hyp 1 in connection with ordinary finite groups. The p.6 comment asks about covering as a translation of revêtement and its possible confusion with covering in a topology; this page ends mid-sentence at I don't see what. Four marginal annotations and the archival numeral 4 are preserved. No signature, letterhead, typed text, displayed formula, or mathematical diagram appears on this page.
author_checks: I expect this will be a general remark in SGA I
I don't know your final decision on this point.
I don't know the ``new numbering'' of SGA
I must admit that there are still many points which are not satisfactory in the exposition.
Perhaps it would have been nicer to avoid a little longer this assumption.
the proof is long and subtle!
I have hesitated a little bit with the word ``covering'' for ``revêtement''
What do you think about this?

math_reading_decisions: The assertions about quotients for ordinary finite groups, the TDTE III proofs, and the purity theorem are carried as unverified statements of the letter. No external theorem or bibliographical verification was performed.
SGA D is retained from the rounded D-shaped glyph; no mathematically or bibliographically expected replacement is inserted.
TDTE III is read as three Roman uprights, and H is a plain capital. This was visual notation verification only.
The contrast between the translation covering and covering in the étale topology was followed as prose; no equivalence or non-equivalence theorem was checked.
No computation, proof, independent re-proof, or use of a mathematical statement as a proved premise occurred. Therefore check_events is empty.

brief_feedback: The brief does not specify how against_c / against_h should be set when the final preferred reading agrees with a witness but a local uncertainty remains. Here the flags compare the preferred letters and visible state; retained alternatives are recorded separately.
The timing rule was followed conservatively: the exact pre-brief start was not captured, so the first actual clock timestamp is supplied separately.
collation_policy: Substantive differences are counted by physical reading or state. Equivalent spacing, paragraph wrapping, italic-versus-underline encoding with unchanged scope, harmless TikZ geometry, absent handwritten wrappers on this wholly handwritten sheet, and H's omission of the archival comment are excluded. The preferred candidate controls against_c / against_h; uncertainty is explicit in reading.tex and remaining_doubts.
completeness_check: Every manuscript text block, both cancellations, the replacement a, both marginal drawings, the two other margin notes, and the archival numeral have an inventory row and a corresponding representation in reading.tex.
